proofs.title: Atomic allocation and stable numbering
proofs.statement: Acceptance publishes all intended local memberships together and never reuses an allocated number for another article.
proofs.progress_note: Atomic logical publication and stable number/binding lemmas; persistent/reclamation integration remains open. OVER THE SERVED PATH (books/owner-numbering.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-own-served-watermarks-never-decrease -- under fn-own-relation of the configured owner, for any group, any sequence of writer events ((:take), (:begin id), (:store e), (:complete)) through fn-ocfg-step (fn-owner-step, host/owner-host.lisp:209) followed by any connection's outcome installed with fn-ocfg-with-owner (fn-owner-replace-core) leaves the committed view's next local number for that group at least what it was; fn-own-served-local-number-is-never-reassigned -- over the same calls, a (group . number) that names an article of the committed view names an article with the same Message-ID afterwards. The committed view is the archive every reader pins when it opens or advances and reads through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix (owner-host.lisp:1240). Proof: the view is the replay of a prefix of the durable records and the records only grow (fn-own-step-records-prefix); replaying a longer prefix only conses articles on the front and only raises watermarks; the Message-ID half cites fn-state-has-fresh-local-numbers on the new view. Teeth (tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests.lisp): witness of two POSTs in fn.letters across a completion (numbers 3 and 4, watermark 3 to 5, 1 and 2 keep their Message-IDs, the advanced reader's GROUP 211 4 1 4 and STAT 3/4 name the new articles); must-fail for the relation on both keystones (the store node's archive wound back to empty: the 240 is still answered, fn.letters 1 is given again and the watermark falls from 3 to 2) and for the holder hypothesis (fn.letters 3 unheld before, held after). The writer-events hypothesis has no tooth: no violating value was found (every other fn-ocfg-step arm keeps the view or refreshes it from an extension of the records), and redundancy is not proved; it is the statement's scope. SCOPE of fn-own-pinned-view-survives-other-post (T6): reader connections only, by design -- a peer connection answers IHAVE/CHECK from the live node (fn-own-conn-live-session), so a POST by another connection correctly changes its 335 to 435; tests/acl2/owner-served-invariants-tests shows it. No peer-connection variant is owed. proofs.title: Reservation and release safety
proofs.statement: Accepted obligations are accounted for and discharge requires the specified predicate over committed authorized evidence.
proofs.progress_note: Finite abstract admission and general release preserve valid ledgers; release preserves independent pins and known identities. P9 over the host-called functions (books/store-node-retention.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-spc-prepare (host/store-node-host.lisp:472, answered :refused at :475 when it returns its input) returns the live store state unchanged whenever the record's charge exceeds the room the node's retention capacity leaves, with that comparison its only hypothesis; fn-node-prepare does the same; fn-node-prepare-refuses-whatever-retain-admit-refuses is the named equation that makes RET-002's fn-retain-admit-refuses-unaffordable-obligation a statement about the called function (fn-retain-admit's no-op is exactly the inadmissible case, and in that case prepare refuses). fn-sn-finish (store-node-host.lisp:546): every article accepted before a completion is accepted after it on every arm (no hypothesis beyond membership), and an obligation leaves the ledger only when the completed record is a retention release, not an undertaking, matching its id, subject, kind and evidence; Store releases name kind :forward, so no arm releases an article's :archive pin (corollary fn-sn-finish-keeps-every-archive-obligation). Scope: charges are abstract units, not physical bytes; there is no archive-release event in v0, so 'until explicit release' is 'kept' for articles; crash/recover and sweep are not covered here. Authorized/committed evidence validation remains open. M5 transaction budget over the called prepare (books/owner-store-budget.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-sbud-prepare, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare installs, is the identity when the budget is at most the owner Store's committed record count and is fn-opc-prepare below it; its refusal word is :unaffordable; the budget is the persisted profile's admissibility (fn-sbud-budget-is-the-profile-admissibility) and is fixed at init. Byte-level torn writes remain the DESIGN-crash-model-v2 design, which is review finding D4. proofs.title: Compaction and protected closure
proofs.statement: Reclamation and crash-interrupted compaction preserve every dependency rooted by policy and obligations.
proofs.progress_note: The implemented physical tranche retains exact canonical event bytes in one immutable selected pack, validates every surviving covered record, accepts only missing files within the covered prefix, requires a contiguous uncovered suffix, and resumes exact prefix unlink under the writer lease. fn-cc-partial-deletion-preserves-exact-history covers arbitrary missing subsets of that prefix under summary, suffix and exact-observation hypotheses; its test has a non-degenerate middle deletion and one must-fail event per hypothesis. The aggregate parser refuses above 4 MiB before header parsing and its focused test round-trips a valid pack larger than the generic 65538-octet CBOR input cap. Selected namespace and exact-overlap helper guards are verified; guard closure of the actual framed coverage/observation caller remains open on the shared unverified Store-event decoder chain. The definition-unfolding prefix-plus-suffix equality is deliberately not a registry event. One pack is limited to 4096 events and 4 MiB, so this exact-history representation cannot compact arbitrarily large stores. Open: a general crash correspondence theorem, active-reader coordination, protected article-object closure, filesystem qualification, and integrated native-image execution. The byte crash correspondence now transcribes the actual native reclaim plan as repeated transaction-directory unlinks with a post-unlink cut and a closing directory fence with a post-barrier cut. Executable witnesses show arbitrary covered-name survival before the fence, no restoration after it, exact suffix retention, and conflict refusal. The native caller now invokes the logical plan subject directly; recovery continues through fn-store-checkpoint-compaction-observe. Source mapping and model witnesses are not integrated native-image evidence; source-matched process-death execution and filesystem qualification remain open. The actual reclaim planner now uses total nested-pair accessors and has explicit guard events, with source-LD evidence and malformed-input witnesses. The modeled crash examples execute the actual planner through a test helper; no hand-written substitute program supplies their run. These source checks do not certify the complete dependency closure or establish general suffix preservation under all physical crashes. No event yet; T12d (009 stays v1). The scoped ACL2 pack-retirement book proves the selected generation survives every modeled issued-unlink cut under plan-prefix and selected-membership premises, and that a valid gap-aware next generation exceeds the selected name when not exhausted. Its test book supplies a multi-generation deletion witness and counterexamples to the keystone premises. The native caller uses the proved plan under the exclusive Store lock, with one cut after each unlink and one after the packs-directory barrier; an empty plan returns without a cut. The follow-up count theorems state that surviving unlinks reduce bounded pack namespace occupancy, without authorizing retained-history or article-object deletion. Native image execution and syscall/power-loss correspondence remain open.

WHY THIS IS NOT YET `certified`: (a) `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` still has no caller -- no served query walks the slot list; (b) A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification, and the only witnesses are under the toy realiser of `tests/acl2/crypto-seam-tests`; (c) the keyring is supplied per invocation and is not carried in the durable configuration history, so a restart forgets it; and (d) `fn-stx-transit-authority-ok` (books/stx-policy) still walks the whole lace per article on the ADMISSION path and has no caller, so D3 is answered at the query and not at admission. proofs.title: Live reconfiguration: what a configuration generation serves, and what a crash recovers (R5, T8)
proofs.statement: fn-ocl-no-reader-observes-a-half-change, over what the host calls (staging through fn-ocfg-step at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas, publication through fn-ocl-publish at fn-owner-reconfigure-complete) and with no hypothesis: every open connection's record, every configuration pin and every served table are unchanged across staging and publication; staging leaves the live configuration where it was; a non-durable verdict changes nothing; a :durable verdict completes exactly the record whose generation the durable write named, appends that whole record to the store's configuration history, publishes what that history replays to, clears the stage and installs the matching posting configuration. The owner itself is not unchanged on the called path (store and posting configuration move). fn-ocl-publish-installs-the-whole-staged-record: under fn-ocl-config-historyp the published configuration is fn-cfg-apply-record of the live configuration and the whole staged record, by fn-ocl-cpr-loop-configuration-is-the-record-fold. fn-ocl-publish-agrees-with-ocfg-complete-on-readers equates the called path with the model event (:complete) on pins, served tables, connection records and the stage. fn-ocl-request-refused-over-a-reader-in-the-group: a group request (fn-ocl-request-deltas, the delta the host no longer builds) for a group some open connection's reader has selected is refused at staging. The model statement follows. fn-ocfg-no-reader-observes-a-half-change: the two owner events a live reconfiguration consists of, (:reconfigure other deltas) then (:complete), leave the owner -- every open connection's record, session and pinned archive, hence every reply -- and every configuration pin exactly as they were; staging leaves the live configuration where it was; and publication moves it to fn-ocfg-published-config of the staged record, the old configuration or fn-cfg-apply-record of the whole record and nothing between; one hypothesis, that a record was staged, the condition under which the host calls (:complete). fn-ocfg-pin-is-stable-without-advance: over any finite fn-ocfg-step event list holding no (:advance id), (:close id) or (:fault id), a pinned connection keeps the configuration it opened at. fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation, over what the host calls (staging (:reconfigure id deltas) and (:close id) through fn-ocfg-step, the durable write, publication through fn-ocl-publish; recovery through fn-cpr-replay of the configuration journal and the Store journal at host/owner-host.lisp:173 in fn-owner-recover), with one hypothesis, fn-ocl-config-historyp (the live configuration is what fn-cpr-replay of the store's own journals recovers): before the durable write the store and both journals are unchanged and replay :ok to the live configuration, which staging did not move; after the write and before publication, a replay of the configuration journal with the staged record appended is either not :ok (the host answers :fault and installs nothing) or recovers exactly the configuration the model's (:complete) publishes, fn-cfg-apply-record of the live configuration and the whole record, at the record's generation; on a :durable publication the installed store's journals are exactly those, their replay is :ok to the published configuration, nothing is staged and the hypothesis holds again, so the statement chains across every later reconfiguration; A-DURABILITY enters as the publisher's :durable meaning the record is in the directory the next open reads. fn-ocl-cpr-replay-ok-is-config-replay-ok relates the called replay to the configuration-only one as a refinement: an :ok of fn-cpr-replay on (configs, events) is an :ok of fn-cnode-config-replay on configs with the same configuration; the converse is false (a configuration journal whose transaction ids descend is accepted by fn-cnode-config-replay and refused :config-txid by fn-cpr-replay; tests/acl2/config-crash-replay-tests), and the called path does not write such a journal (fn-cpo-configure-durable appends only at the Store frontier and only when fn-cpr-replay of the result is :ok). The model statements fn-ocfg-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation and fn-ocfg-config-replay-of-one-more-record (books/owner-config.lisp, over fn-cnode-config-replay, which no host line calls, and fn-ocfg-step (:complete)) stay as model-level lemmas and are not registry events. fn-ocfg-open-pins-the-live-configuration and fn-ocfg-advance-observes-the-live-configuration: under fn-ocfg-statep a new or advanced connection pins the live configuration. fn-native-admin-live-group-delta-is-a-typed-delta: an accepted group create or retire stages one delta that fn-cfg-deltap admits. Covered scope: the owner's configuration and pins; NOT covered: the live node's allocation domain and capacity, which no owner transition moves, so a group created live is published and in the injection configuration but GROUP and LIST ACTIVE answer from the acceptance state's group list and do not show it until a restart (books/owner-config.lisp OPEN item 3); LIST ACTIVE on the wire answers from that list, not from the pin (OPEN item 1).

proofs.title: The outbound feed offers exactly the peers in scope, and never a loop (K2, outbound half)
proofs.statement: fn-own-feed-target-is-offerable with fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer: for a feed table the owner carries, the peers one durably accepted article is offered to are exactly the peers of that table whose own configured record has an outbound half, whose outbound wildmat matches one of the article's own Newsgroups names, whose path-identity the article's Path does not already name, and which is not the peer the article arrived from. fn-own-feed-never-offers-a-loop is the loop-freedom half (RFC 5537 section 3.6) and fn-own-feed-target-is-in-scope the scope half; fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin transport both to the table the owner holds, and fn-own-feed-tick-peer-is-the-feed-tick is the subject rule tying one peer's tick to fn-feed-tick-step on that peer's own feed. Covered scope: one article's octets against one table; the hypothesis is the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep. NOT covered: the statement over fn-own-step and fn-feedp preservation, which is cited from books/peer-feed-invariants and not restated. Over the functions the host calls (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-own-submission-targets-are-feed-targets bounds fn-own-submission-targets -- what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent reaches through fn-own-submission-intent-records, and what fn-own-feed-durable enqueues and fn-own-feed-durable-records journals -- by fn-own-feed-targets (a bound, not an equation: a peer already holding the Message-ID is filtered out); fn-own-submission-never-targets-a-loop is the loop statement over it under the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep; fn-own-transit-outcome-never-enqueues-on-the-origin says the owner fn-owner-transit-outcome installs keeps the origin peer's feed unchanged, whatever the decision and the store word. fn-own-feed-accept has no caller in books/ or host/, so fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin are -sibling theorems and count for nothing on their own; the host-called replacements are fn-own-feed-durable-touches-only-the-submission-targets and fn-own-feed-durable-never-enqueues-on-the-origin. fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer's recognizer and bound-entry hypotheses are redundant (tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests proves the conclusion from the scope decision alone), so it has one tooth, not three.

proofs.title: Provenance is typed, and its wire form is lossless and legacy-compatible
proofs.statement: Every string is an admissible provenance (the :legacy kind), so widening the retention evidence slot from stringp to fn-provp changes no stored value; the rendered form of each typed kind is exactly the string that kind's writer produced before the widening; and a provenance the codec can write is the provenance it reads back from its wire form.
proofs.note: The transit path's DURABLE provenance is not covered: fn-peer-injection-arguments still passes fn-peer-evidence's rendering, and fn-peer-evidence-is-the-legacy-rendering is the equation between the typed record and that string, not evidence that the record reaches the store. books/peer-inbound and books/peer-inbound-invariants have no certificate on dev (blocked on fn-peer-echo-reply-effects-well-formed), so those two events are admitted, not certified, and are not listed here.

proofs.title: AUTHINFO on the served path, and what posting follows (W10)
proofs.statement: fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed: with authentication required and no authenticated subject, a restricted command's step submits nothing, never offers article mode, leaves the session unchanged and its whole effect list is the single 480 line (RFC 4643 section 2.2). Its seven hypotheses each have a violating value in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp; the two syntactic ones it used to carry were removed on 2026-09-22 because no value violates them while the restricted-keyword hypothesis holds (fn-auth-restricted-keyword-is-a-keyword-token). fn-auth-post-without-permission-is-not-offered and its lift fn-auth-step-post-without-permission-is-not-offered: a connection whose posting allowance is false is answered by this book and never offered 340, so no body can follow and no submission can leave; fn-auth-postingp is the authenticated principal's credential flag, so a principal enrolled without it is refused 440 however permissive the pinned injection configuration is (RFC 3977 6.3.1.1). fn-served-dispatch-of-a-refused-post-leaves-the-wire-in-place carries that to the served dispatcher: the wire is not switched into article mode and the read carries no submission. fn-auth-pass-before-user-is-482 and fn-auth-failed-pass-leaves-the-session-unauthenticated are two of the three RFC 4643 section 2.3.2 codes, each with the session unchanged or cleared. The third is stated over the called function: fn-auth-step-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls says that while the operator's policy is protected-only and the connection carries no TLS layer, an AUTHINFO command line -- USER or PASS, any arguments, configured name or not -- is answered 483 and nothing else happens: the session is the one the command arrived on, so no name is cached and no subject is installed, no submission leaves, and the secret is never compared because the branch that would compare it is not reached. Its eight hypotheses each have a violating value in the teeth book. The label half of the same channel: fn-auth-starttls-is-not-advertised-under-tls-on-any-connection, fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated-on-any-connection and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-before-tls-under-protected-only are over fn-auth-capability-lines-for-peer, which is the list fn-auth-command puts in the 101 block for EVERY connection and not only a reader's, and fn-auth-step-capability-block-unfolds-to-the-peer-aware-lines is the named unfold equating that list to what fn-auth-step emits; fn-auth-starttls-is-not-advertised-without-a-certificate is the reader-facing instance of the first. Those three say what a client is OFFERED; they do not state anything about the octets fn-nntp-multi renders the list into. fn-auth-pass-accepts-only-a-checking-secret says the accepting branch ran fn-authsec-checkp against the stored verifier; it does NOT say a wrong secret fails, which is A-CRYPTO. Covered scope: one served connection over a pinned archive and a pinned AUTHINFO configuration. The subject of the lifts above is fn-auth-step, a sibling the host does not call: books/served.lisp:617 fn-served-dispatch calls fn-auth-step-pinned, which host/owner-host.lisp:1240 fn-owner-chunk reaches through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix. P1 is stated over that called function and over fn-served-dispatch, each 480 and 483 statement proved from the fn-auth-step keystone and the bridge fn-auth-step-pinned-agrees-with-auth-step-on-handled-command: fn-auth-step-pinned-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed (seven hypotheses, the 480 keystone's) and fn-served-dispatch-of-a-gated-command-is-480-and-changes-nothing, which says that on a served connection whose policy requires authentication and which has no subject, a restricted command within the command and argument bounds leaves the whole connection (wire framing, session, pinned archive and indexes) equal to the one it arrived on and its only effect is the 480 line; fn-auth-step-pinned-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls (eight hypotheses) and fn-served-dispatch-of-authinfo-on-a-clear-connection-is-483-and-changes-nothing, the same for AUTHINFO on a clear connection under protected-only, whose only effect is the 483 line, so no name is cached and the secret is never compared; fn-auth-step-pinned-post-by-a-principal-without-the-flag-is-440, an authenticated principal whose credential lacks the posting flag is answered 440 to POST with the session unchanged and no submission; and fn-auth-step-pinned-post-by-a-principal-with-the-flag-is-delegated, one whose credential carries the flag and whose principal is the subject has its POST handed unchanged to fn-auth-delegate-pinned, where the pinned injection configuration still decides. Each has its hypotheses dropped one at a time under must-fail with an evaluated counterexample in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp (keystones 11 to 17). Covered scope: one dispatched command event; the chain from fn-served-dispatch to the host read is fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix and fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read. OB-AUTH-FOLD is fn-auth-fold-step-has-no-local-submission: if the served connection is valid, its pinned credential policy grants posting to no principal, and no local POST body is pending, every effect of the complete fn-served-step read excludes fn-inj-injectedp; fn-auth-fold-step-preserves-safe-connp carries those conditions between reads. Separately authorized fn-peer-submissionp transit remains possible, as the reachable AUTHINFO plus TAKETHIS witness shows. The invoked subject is fn-served-step, reached by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read; fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix is its named correspondence.
proofs.progress_note: Historical W10 local admission and cache-origin limitations are superseded for the frozen03 closure and source-pinned native-auth continuation by their archived certification/build evidence. The native AUTHINFO startup receiver passes scoped live wrong-password/correct-password and reader-versus-peer cases. These results do not establish independent-client interoperability, native protected transport, or complete physical adapter correspondence. Native principal administration has scoped ACL2 and actual replacement/recovery evidence; public CLI composition remains open. The existing salted SHA-256 verifier is preserved without a password-hardening or secrecy theorem claim. Lane t7/auth-teeth, 2026-09-22: the events above are curated for the first time and tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp is the teeth book, with a reachable non-degenerate witness for each keystone and one must-fail per hypothesis for the 480 gate (seven) and the 483 refusal (eight), plus separating witnesses for the three capability labels. OB-AUTH-FOLD now proves the local-submission exclusion through the served byte fold in books/nntp-auth-fold.lisp, with a reachable transit counterexample to the prior no-any-submission claim. Two of K1's four hypotheses (fn-served-connp and the not-handshaking one) are proof-support and have no must-fail, because K1 restated without them reaches an open case, a session that is fn-auth-sessionp but not consistent with its connection's archive. The 483-before-TLS and 281-after-STARTTLS behaviour on a deployed image is tools/node_probe.py's row and has not been run on one. K2 follow-up teeth isolate the no-pending-POST premise with a forged but fn-served-connp no-posters state after an actual 340 offer; it submits locally and is unreachable from a no-posters open under the preservation theorem. fn-served-connp is a structural carried connection invariant, not a separate permission test or a runtime whole-store scan.

proofs.title: The recovery window's crash images are kernel-admissible and risk no acknowledged record
proofs.statement: In the recovery window -- the phases between a process replaying what it scanned from the view and completing its five recovery fences -- a crash may drop the record the replay read, because that record's directory entry is the entry operation a dead process left pending; and it may roll the frontier back, because the pending entry operation may be the allocator rename instead. fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits exactly those two images and no other, each gated by an empty success history, the frontier arm additionally by a record list that leaves the reserved txid unused, and the two exclusive of one another; every image it admits is produced by fn-sf-image-crash with the same frontier, records, :replaying phase and success history; and an acknowledged pair of the pre-crash state names a record of EVERY image it admits, both rolled-back ones included.
proofs.note: Decisions D14-b (lane w10/kernel-freedom, the record arm) and D14-c (lane w11/bytestore-k2, the frontier arm K2f). The recognizer is a SECOND one: fn-sf-crash-imagep is unchanged and stays the reliance predicate that fn-own-reopen gates on and every reopen theorem takes as a premise, because widening it is false for the composition -- an owner reopened on an image is a recovery-window state whose own success history is empty while its ledger names records earlier processes acknowledged, and which of a state's records are fenced is a fact about the byte store's pending list, not about the kernel state. The counterexample is mechanized in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the owner half) and tests/acl2/store-observed-traces-tests.lisp (the kernel half). proofs.title: A clock the host contradicts is dropped, and the refusal is not an article verdict
proofs.statement: fn-own-observe answers exactly one of :observed, :refused and :invalid, and the host reports that word rather than inferring one from a state comparison. On a related owner a :refused reading names a host contradiction -- the monotonic counter went backwards, has-wall changed, or a widened error bound moved the earliest admissible true time back -- and never merely a reading that did not move, because a reading equal to the one held is admitted. A refusal leaves the owner with no clock, and with no usable injection reading fn-nntp-post-step emits no submission and answers `441 posting failed; this server has no usable clock reading', which is a different constant from every article verdict the step can give.

Keystones fn-own-observe-refusal-names-a-contradiction (books/owner-invariants.lisp) and fn-post-without-a-clock-refuses-with-the-clock-line (books/nntp-post.lisp), with fn-own-observe-outcome-is-one-of-three and fn-own-observe-outcome-decides-the-clock-by-definition named for what they are and cited by :use. proofs.title: A reopened journal answers for a work what the pre-crash machine would have, and says which works it recovered
proofs.statement: fn-bp-work-status-of-restart: under fn-bp-statep, the :restart transition a reopen runs changes the boundary answer for one work id by fn-bp-work-status-after-restart and by nothing else -- an attempt that was in flight is marked :restart-observed, while :absent, :outstanding, :receipted, a retryable status and :delivered are fixed points. fn-bp-replay-work-status-is-the-pre-crash-status-restarted lifts that to fn-bp-replay-journal, the predecessor interpreter for the original FNWF kinds: when the replay succeeds, fn-bp-work-status of the installed image is fn-bp-work-status-after-restart of fn-bp-work-status of the trace of the initial state over fn-bp-durable-events, the journal's denotation without that trailing restart. Provenance is separate and also ACL2's: fn-bp-work-origin-at-open-is-recovered-or-absent says that against the id list fn-bp-work-ids records at open, every work the image holds reads :recovered and every other id reads :absent; fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued says this session's durable enqueue of an id that list does not name reads :enqueued. So a work recovered from a cut and a work enqueued after the reopen, which share the status :outstanding, are distinct at the boundary. fn-bprl-replay-work-status-is-durable-status-restarted covers fn-bprl-replay-journal over the release-aware FNWF language: if replay succeeds, the installed work status is the one-restart status of the exact ACL2 release-aware interpreter folded over its durable records.

proofs.title: The frame integrity trailer has one owner, and the host's framing is the model's
proofs.statement: fn-frame-trailer (books/frame-trailer.lisp) is the only definition of the 32-octet frame integrity trailer in the tree: it is fn-frame-digest, realised by fn-sha256 through books/crypto-attach.lisp, and it answers :bad rather than a digest for an argument that is not an octet list. For any magic, version, kind and payload in fn-frame-inputp, the byte string a host builds by asking ACL2 for the protected prefix, asking ACL2 for the trailer over it and concatenating the two is fn-frame-seal of those fields; and handing that byte string back to fn-frame-decode with the trailer re-derived over the frame's own fn-frame-protected-prefix answers fn-frame-ok of the fields that went in. The same two statements hold for the store instance the bridge executes, over fn-frame-store-protected and fn-frame-store-decode. Collision and preimage resistance are A-CRYPTO and are not claimed: the attachment introduces no axiom and the seam's constraints are shape only.
proofs.note: Lane w11/one-owner. Keystones fn-frame-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal, fn-frame-decode-of-host-framing and their store instances fn-frame-store-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal and fn-frame-store-decode-of-host-framing, all in books/frame-trailer.lisp. Subject-to-host: the host lines that call fn-frame-trailer are tools/frame_bridge.py FrameSession.trailer (called by seal and digest_of), host/native/io.lisp fnn-trailer (called by fnn-seal and fnn-digest-of) and tools/run_owner.py Acl2Owner.trailer (called by feed_frames and feed_replay_frame); each replaced a separate SHA-256 in that host. Teeth in tests/acl2/frame-trailer-tests.lisp: 25 assert-events, including two FIPS 180-4 vectors, the exact store prefix and trailer octets, the :bad boundary arm, and one violating value per clause (a magic whose third octet is 300 for the shape clause keystone 1 needs, a max-payload of 2 for the bound clause keystone 2 needs, and a non-octet record for the store instance). Byte identity with the deleted host copies was cross-checked outside ACL2 against CPython hashlib.sha256 at 32, 4096, 32768, 262144 and 1048576 octets. NOT closed by this target: fn-frame-digest's collision resistance, and the marshalling cost of sealing a 4 MiB staged inbound bundle through the decimal-octet bridge.
proofs.progress_note: Both books certified with tools/certify_books.py on the laptop (ACL2 8.7, SBCL 2.6.8), evidence dirs above. The four keystones and the 25 assert-events all pass. proofs.title: Prefix and lower-frontier recoverability of a replayed history
proofs.statement: A history that replays successfully leaves an IDLE node whose next txid only moves forward, so dropping its last record leaves a history recoverable at the same frontier, and a history whose txids are all below a bound is recoverable AT that bound. Those are the two facts fn-sf-history-recoverablep needs beyond a successful replay -- together they are fn-replay-advance-okp -- and on them every image the platform may leave in the recovery window is replayable at its own frontier and the host's reopen entry succeeds on it.

The acknowledged-record half of crash-model-v2 K4 is NOT restated over the wider predicate: on both rollback arms the arm's own (null (fn-sf-successes s)) and a member-equal success hypothesis are contradictory, so the restatement would be fn-sn-acknowledged-record-survives-observed-reopen with two vacuous arms. fn-sf-recovery-admissible-image-facts carries that guarantee over every arm instead. proofs.title: Checkpoint validation refuses a non-journal prefix
proofs.statement: Checkpoint validation binds a checkpoint to exactly one prefix and refuses a prefix that is not an ordered journal interval below the checkpoint frontier: fn-cpc-validp implies the checkpoint is fn-checkpoint-capture-value of that prefix at its frontier, and a prefix with any record whose recorded generation is not its transaction id is refused for every checkpoint and configuration offered with it.

proofs.title: The BPv7 bundle codec inverts, and what fn authors another implementation accepts
proofs.statement: For every bundle satisfying fn-bpb-bundlep whose encoding is within the caller's transfer bound, fn-bpb-decode of fn-bpb-encode is that same bundle and nothing else (fn-bpb-decode-of-encode), resting on the one-block round trip fn-bpb-decode-block-of-encode-block, the fold over the block sequence fn-bpb-decode-blocks-of-encode-blocks and the primary block's half fn-bpb-scan-primary-of-encode; every accepted input yields a bundle (fn-bpb-decode-yields-bundle) and an input over the bound is refused before any octet is examined (fn-bpb-decode-refuses-overlong-input). Over those, the node's two ends: what fn-bpn-send puts on the wire is a bundle (fn-bpn-send-bundle-is-a-bundle), and a peer that accepts what fn-bpn-send authored recovers exactly the ADU that was sent (fn-bpn-receive-of-send-carries-the-adu), under the receiver's own configuration and transfer limit. The covered scope is a whole bundle with at most *fn-bpb-max-blocks* canonical blocks plus the payload block; fragments, BPSec and status reports are outside it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bp-node, 2026-09-21; the codec keystones are lane w10/dtn-3's. The EXTERNAL check is *bpb-dtn7-0-21-0*: 132 octets dtn7-rs 0.21.0 authored, which fn decodes and re-encodes byte for byte (planning/evidence/bp-dtn7-w11-2026-09-21.md). proofs.title: Every connection the owner opens carries the operator's AUTHINFO policy, and its greeting says what that policy allows
proofs.statement: fn-served-peer-and-reader-open-under-the-same-policy: the AUTHINFO configuration pinned into a connection the owner resolved to a peer record (fn-served-open-peer) is the same value pinned into a reader connection opened under that policy (fn-served-open), so no decision in books/nntp-auth.lisp -- the credential fn-auth-authinfo searches, the AUTHINFO and STARTTLS labels fn-auth-capability-lines emits, the 480 gate fn-auth-gatedp applies and the posting allowance fn-auth-postingp computes -- can answer one way for a client the owner resolved as a peer and another way for the client beside it. fn-served-open-peer-pins-the-configuration is the field-level half: the pinned value is the argument, coerced by fn-auth-open-session to fn-auth-open-config only when it is not a configuration. fn-auth-step-preserves-the-config is what makes those two statements about the CONNECTION and not only about its open: for any session and any wire event, with no hypothesis at all, the step's session carries the same fn-auth-session-config -- not a login, not the handshake, not a delegated reader command and not a command books/nntp-auth.lisp does not answer writes that field. Every decision in that book reads it, so the policy a client meets on its hundredth command is the one pinned before the connection opened. Covered scope: the OPEN transition for the first two, and one step for the third; the fold over a whole read is OB-AUTH-FOLD's. The subject is what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open-peer calls through fn-own-open-peer, which tools/run_owner.py Owner.accept_nntp calls for every accepted socket whose source address matches a peer record. Second half, the same value read where a client first sees it: fn-served-open-greets-200-exactly-when-the-connection-may-post says the greeting the open emits is RFC 3977 section 5.1.2's 200 exactly when the pinned injection configuration allows posting AND fn-auth-postingp of the session just built is true -- which is the conjunction fn-auth-command hands fn-nntp-capability-lines for the POST label and the one fn-auth-postingp decides 340 against 440 and 480 by. fn-served-open-greeting-agrees-with-the-post-label states that over the octets a client sees, and is named for what it is: a corollary of the keystone and a local unfold of fn-auth-capability-lines, doing no work of its own. Covered scope: the OPEN transition. It says nothing about the greeting a connection would deserve LATER, after a 281 changes the allowance; RFC 4643 section 2.2 sends the client back to CAPABILITIES for that, and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated is the only statement fn has about the block after a login. After the open: fn-auth-step-pinned-login-installs-the-credential-posting-flag says that for any wire event, a step of the host-called fn-auth-step-pinned that takes a session with no subject to one with a subject leaves a posting allowance (fn-auth-postingp) equal to the posting flag of the credential enrolled under the session's cached name; covered scope: one step.
proofs.note: Lane w11/auth-live, decided by measurement and not by inspection. fn-served-open-peer pinned the literal (fn-auth-open-config) while fn-served-open pinned the operator's, and the owner resolves a connection to a peer by SOURCE ADDRESS alone, so on a box where a configured peer is reachable on loopback every client was opened without the operator's policy: AUTHINFO PASS answered 481 with the secret just written, CAPABILITIES carried no AUTHINFO line and POST was never gated. Both theorems are FALSE of that definition. The live before/after is planning/evidence/auth-live-2026-09-21.md and the boundary test is tests/test_auth.py ServedCredentialTests, which starts the node with `bin/fn run` over an fn.toml and writes the peer record, because no test that starts tools/run_owner.py directly can reach this. The greeting half is a second defect the same measurement found: fn-served-greeting read the injection configuration alone, so a connection under [auth] required = true greeted 200 and then answered POST 480, where section 5.1.2's MUST is 201. It takes the opened session now. Lane t7/auth-teeth, 2026-09-22: teeth in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp. Neither greeting theorem nor either pinning theorem has a hypothesis, so the teeth are the values that separate the two sides together with a must-fail on the statement the definition satisfied BEFORE the 2026-09-21 measurement: that the greeting is 200 exactly when the injection configuration allows posting, and that the peer open pins (fn-auth-open-config). fn-served-open-greeting-agrees-with-the-post-label stays uncited: the statement above names it a corollary and a local unfold, so its evidence is the witnesses on both sides of its iff, not a registry event. fn-auth-step-preserves-the-config is new in this lane and was asked for by name in the header of books/nntp-auth-invariants.lisp as the first of the three facts OB-AUTH-FOLD waits on.

Native configured-peer/source admission and protected transport remain separate; this does not extend the OPEN theorem to every subsequent connection transition.

proofs.title: A host fault costs one connection, and the fourth outcome says so
proofs.statement: fn-own-fault (books/owner-fault.lisp) is the owner's host-fault transition. For any owner and any connection id: the faulted connection is no longer found; every connection with a different id is EQUAL to what it was, so every later step over it has the same input it would have had; a submission in flight for the faulted id, and a pending transaction held by it, are cleared, with no hypothesis that the connection was still open, while a submission in flight for a DIFFERENT id is untouched; the store, the committed view and the completion ledger are unchanged; and the octets the faulted connection receives are RFC 3977 section 3.2.1's 403 and are not the reply octets of fn-nntp-post-outcome for any session and any completion, including that function's own malformed-session 403 -- so the fault is a fourth outcome, distinguishable on the wire from accepted, refused and uncertain.
proofs.note: Lane w11/owner-survival. CLAIMED as PRF-035 and renumbered to PRF-040 on merging dev: 035 had already gone to w11/one-owner's frame trailer, 036 to w11/bytestore-k2, 037 to w11/checkpoint-validator, 038 to w11/bp-node and 039 to w11/auth-live, all inside one evening. Keystones fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection, fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and fn-own-fault-reply-is-not-a-post-outcome (books/owner-fault.lisp), with fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission, fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction and fn-own-fault-is-not-a-store-event beside them. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp on the same witness the served POST scenario builds (*own-taken*: connection 4's submission in flight, reader 3 open), including one violating value per hypothesis and the relation holding after a fault. The host side is tests/test_owner.py OwnerSurvivesAFaultTests, which injects an unexpected exception on one connection and asserts the other is still served. TEETH (tests/acl2/owner-fault-tests.lisp, 2026-09-24): every owner-fault event above has a reachable witness on *own-taken*, and one must-fail per violable hypothesis: fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection 1 (other = id), fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission 1 (the in-flight submission is another connection's), fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission 1 (it is the faulted connection's), fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction 1 (a reader faults while connection 4 holds the transaction; the review had found no violating value). REDUNDANT HYPOTHESES: the (fn-own-inflight o) hypothesis of fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and of fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission can never be violated usefully -- with nothing in flight the slot stays empty -- and the test book proves both conclusions without it (oft-clears-the-faulted-submission-needs-only-the-id, oft-keeps-another-connections-submission-needs-only-the-id). The statements keep the hypothesis; removing it is a later decision. fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, -is-not-a-store-event and -reply-is-not-a-post-outcome have no hypothesis and carry a witness only. EVIDENCE: persvati run-20260924T152544Z-e3c9, manifest planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260924T152627Z-1775721.json: tests/acl2/owner-fault-tests passed, 4.0 s (books/owner-fault unchanged). OPEN under this target: nothing states that the HOST calls fn-own-fault at every point where it can fault -- the boundary's coverage is a code property, not a theorem -- and tools/run_reader.py has no such boundary at all. Native host calls fn-owner-fault through fnn-owner-serialized/fault-service, but at checkpoint 76901c1 also stops the service for unexpected serious conditions. The logical single-connection theorem does not establish native service survival; that actual-host obligation remains open. Shared-core failure and uncertain persistence require a global fence and are not justified as connection-local faults by this theorem.

proofs.title: Every byte-level crash image of a related store scans, and scans to an image the file kernel admits
proofs.statement: fn-bs-store-crash-image-scans (K1): for every byte store related to a file-kernel state and every image fn-bs-crash-imagep admits of it, the scan tools/run_store.py performs at open -- the config entry and its integrity check, the frontier entry and its decode, the contiguity of the transaction namespace, and the record list -- returns :ok and not any of its four :fault values. No trailer assumption is used: an authority inode is fenced before any name points at it (D1) and is never overwritten (D2), so the only freedom a crash has over the authority namespace is whether the last entry operation landed. fn-bs-store-crash-image-is-kernel-admissible (K2): what that scan reads is an image fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits, which outside the recovery window is the reliance predicate fn-sf-crash-imagep and inside it is that plus the two rollback arms of D14-b and D14-c -- the record the replay read and has not re-fenced, and the allocator rename that the fourth recovery barrier has not drained. fn-bs-store-recovery-is-a-kernel-crash (K3): fn-sf-image-crash at that image reproduces its frontier, its record list and the :replaying phase. fn-bs-crash-image-consumer-replay-ok: from the maintained E2 completed-prefix relation fn-csi-full-relationp, K2 and the platform crash-image arms, the exact scanned record list strictly replays the consumer projection, including recovery rollback. fn-bs-crash-image-reopens: the host reopen entry fn-sn-open-observed succeeds on every such image whose identity and topic histories replay (fn-sn-observed-identity-okp and fn-sn-observed-topic-okp), with E2 consumer replay derived rather than assumed. fn-bs-acknowledged-record-survives-byte-crash (K4): under the same maintained and observed conditions, an acknowledged outcome names a reopened record. K-sweep: fn-bs-staging-unlink-keeps-relation-and-scan, an unlink in :staging at any name and with any outcome keeps the byte relation to the same kernel state and keeps the scan; fn-bs-recover-sweep-keeps-relation-at-every-cut, every pair of fn-bs-recover-sweep-program's run (every recovery-stage-unlinked cut) is that kernel state with a related byte state and the original scan; fn-bs-sweep-round-keeps-every-cut-reopenable, over the names fn-sn-sweep-round returns (host/native/io.lisp fnn-sweep-staging via fn-store-sn-sweep-round), every identity- and topic-replayable crash image at every cut of the sweep reopens and the kernel state is the one before the sweep. The sweep's rounds (books/store-sweep.lisp): fn-sn-sweep-rounds-collect-every-orphan, with the kernel gate open and a positive observation bound, a staging directory of N unheld staging names ends :done and empty for every N; fn-sn-sweep-rounds-keep-every-name-they-may-not-remove; fn-sn-sweep-rounds-end-done-or-refused, the loop ends :done or :refused and :refused means more than one observation of names remains and that observation removes nothing. K5 scan-record form: fn-bs-stable-prefix-retained-by-byte-crash, under the same byte/kernel relation and modeled crash-image premise, retains the durable decoded record list as a prefix and bounds the scanned list to at most one additional record. K6 partial raw-frame form: fn-bs-k6-actual-record-linked-input-has-exact-frame proves that a well-formed byte state, ACL2-valid record input, fresh staging key, and absent final name at the file-fence cut make the actual P-RECORD linked cut point that final name at the new fenced inode containing the complete supplied frame; the modeled surviving-name crash image at both the actual linked and record-attempted cuts now reads exact raw octets and the decoder returns the candidate; the related-input trace derives no-prior-operation and final-name absence at the file cut for typed Store events; the actual pair-10 whole-list scanner result is now proved conditionally on relation of that pair, while universal relation preservation remains K0. Under a related ready byte/owner input, typed successor frontier frame and fresh staging name, the actual failed P-FRONTIER pair 12 of fn-bs-run is an EIO byte cut for each modeled pending-root-entry choice; the host-called configured-owner :store/:io error observation fences the Store projection while retaining fn-bs-store-relation. The :apply choice makes the candidate durable, while :drop keeps the old frontier. The actual configured-owner retention prepare event, built from the live owner sequence and txid plus host text octets, stages that exact event on the prepared branch and leaves a reserved Store unstaged on refusal. Served-entry byte relation and physical filesystem qualification remain separate obligations.
proofs.note: K1/K2 in byte-store-scan and K3/K4 in byte-store-keystones concern every modeled crash image of an already related byte/kernel state. The reopen subject is fn-sn-open-observed, called by host/store-node-host.lisp; native process startup reaches that entry through its wrapper. K4 additionally assumes maintained consumer completed-prefix consistency and observed identity and topic replay. The topic condition is not yet derived for every modeled byte crash image by the maintained Store relation; a valid physical FNST topic-anchor image after consumer bootstrap separates it from identity and consumer replay. Its recovery-window instances are vacuous because there are no current-process successes there; fn-bs-crash-image-reopens covers that window without a success premise. The identity condition has a kernel witness; its distinct byte-level premise witness remains missing. Framed metadata, a nonempty bootstrap/publication trace and a physically framed registration-before-bootstrap counterexample exercise the other composition boundaries.
