REFUSAL: fn-fc-refused-login-closes-without-an-offer: in either login phase, a complete line whose code is not 281 (and, answering USER, not 381) is :refused, which fn-owner-feed-connection-result-kind (owner-host.lisp:1566) reports as :connection-refused and feed-service.lisp:391-395 answers with the peer-local loss and a close; the connection is closed and nothing fed to it afterwards produces a command, a handshake or an offer. WHAT: fn-fc-auth-user-command-sends-the-configured-name-alone and fn-fc-auth-pass-command-sends-the-configured-secret-alone: on a state whose name (secret) is an fn-fap-tokenp true list, the renderer the host calls (owner-host.lisp:1505, 1605, 1610) returns exactly the prefix, the token and CRLF, one line, so a credential cannot carry a second command; fn-fc-decoded-profile-renders-verbatim-in-every-state composes it with what the host does, with no hypothesis: the profile bytes go through fn-fap-decode (feed-service.lisp:172), the decoded fields are installed by fn-fc-initial-auth-state (owner-host.lisp:1484), and in every state any sequence of reads and TLS reports reaches, the USER and PASS lines are the prefix, the decoded field and CRLF. Not proved here: that the profile file is owner-only and bounded (feed-service.lisp:161-168, native integration evidence), the secrecy of the secret on the wire beyond the TLS ordering above, and the loss-to-requeue composition of fn-feed-lost.
proofs.pending_subject: The image gate (plan T9): the matrix's V0-TRANSIT-AUTHINFO-AB/BA and V0-TRANSIT-AUTHINFO-WRONG rows measured on a frozen image. Filesystem ownership and mode checks on the profile remain native integration evidence; the loss-to-requeue composition is PRF-029/K5's (T9a).
proofs.progress_note: T9c, 2026-09-22: events are the five theorems above; the teeth book is tests/acl2/feed-connection-teeth-tests.lisp (for the unconditional composition, the must-fail is the false neighbour: the same claim over a name and secret that did not come through fn-fap-decode, refuted by a name carrying CRLF and a second command). fn-fap-decode-yields-two-renderable-tokens and fn-fap-decode-refusal-yields-no-credential in books/feed-auth-profile.lisp are the decode facts the composition uses. Status stays in-progress until an image measures the matrix rows.

proofs.title: NEWNEWS exactly filters durable acceptance stamps and reads no payload
proofs.statement: fn-nntp-newnews-scan-is-the-acceptance-filter equates the one-pass served scan with an independent quadratic specification that searches later-accepted articles for the nearest natural stamp, proving soundness and completeness of the conservative legacy horizon and wildmat scope. fn-nntp-newnews-scan-reads-no-payload proves erasing all article payload octets leaves the answer unchanged; fn-nntp-newnews-scan-lines-at-most-candidates bounds the output by matching available articles; fn-nntp-newnews-lines-are-clean proves every line is safe to render. fn-nntp-step-dispatches-newnews-to-the-newnews-response is the subject equation for the host-called dispatcher; fn-nntp-newnews-response-preserves-session and fn-nntp-effects-newnews-response carry the response through the served effect path. Covered scope: one reader session on a pinned committed archive, with a natural schema-1 acceptance stamp or the conservative schema-0 horizon. One command costs O(A*Gprime) for A committed articles and Gprime matched groups, reads no payload and emits at most C lines for C candidates. The true-time no-miss claim for legacy articles assumes A-CLOCK and is outside this theorem.
proofs.note: At this source, green_check finds books/nntp-newnews green at its exact include closure in certify-20260923T232942Z-484654, its test book green in certify-20260924T005919Z-653679, books/nntp-invariants green in certify-20260923T232820Z-480447, and books/nntp-effects green in certify-20260923T232942Z-484654; none has moved dependencies. These are archived certification records, not a current native image qualification. The earlier T2b affected-closure run is certify-20260923T170842Z-2026382; native served-reader validation remains separate.

proofs.title: The operator's post is injected as a served POST is, and its retry is the stored article
proofs.statement: fn-own-operator-submission-is-an-injection-of-the-payload: if fn-own-operator-submit-result answers :submitted, fn-own-operator-submit queues exactly one control submission whose decision is injected, carries the Message-ID and newsgroup list the command named, and whose octets are a re-injection of the submitted octets by the owner's injecting agent (fn-inj-reinjectionp: the agent's Path line, an Injection-Date, the agent's Injection-Info, optionally the generated Message-ID and Date lines, then the submitted octets unchanged); fn-own-operator-decision-is-an-injection-of-the-payload states the same of the decision for any configuration, clock and node. fn-own-operator-submit-without-a-clock-refuses-and-changes-nothing: with no clock observation, or one without a wall time, the result is :refused and the owner is unchanged (D10-a). fn-own-operator-retry-resubmits-the-stored-injection: if fn-inj-decide injected the octets under one clock with that Message-ID and the node holds exactly those injected octets under it, then under any later usable clock the decision is those stored octets, so the store answers the Message-ID's duplicate rather than a conflict. All three rest on fn-inj-injected-article-is-a-reinjection-of-its-source (books/injection-invariants.lisp): every article fn-inj-decide injects is a re-injection of its source by its configured agent, for every clock reading. Covered scope: the owner's decision and its queue entry; the store attempt that follows is the served POST's, and the duplicate decision the store answers is fn-sn-existing-action (books/store-node.lisp), whose exact outcome is stated in store-node-existing-invariants; a single theorem composing this operator retry through the host-called Store attempt is still open. The subject is what the host calls: fn-own-operator-submit through the (:operator-submit ...) event, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-operator-submit steps and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized calls for `fn operator CONFIG post`.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the INN lab's finding 1 (operator post fed INN an article with no Path; 437). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-operator-tests.lisp builds the lab's own operator article through a real owner (configure, observe, submit, take, the store events, the completion) and asserts the queued octets byte for byte against the Path, Injection-Date and Injection-Info lines the lab's served POST carried; one must-fail per hypothesis with a refuting value beside it (the retry keystone through a macro that first admits the full statement). The native tests that run it on an image (tests/test_native_control.py) have not run: no image carries this yet.

proofs.title: An injected article's From is an RFC 5322 mailbox-list (RFC 5536 3.1.2)
proofs.statement: fn-mbx-mailbox-list-names-an-address: every value fn-mbx-mailbox-listp accepts contains an "@" octet, the addr-spec every mailbox carries. fn-inj-injected-proto-article-has-a-mailbox-list-from: whenever fn-inj-decide injects, the From field of the parsed proto-article is accepted by fn-mbx-mailbox-listp and names an address, so `From: yue` (answered 240 and served on 2026-09-22) is refused :from-invalid with `441 posting failed; From is not a valid mailbox list`. fn-mbx-mailbox-listp is RFC 5322 section 3.4's mailbox-list under RFC 5536 sections 2.1 and 2.2 (no obsolete syntax but obs-phrase, US-ASCII), bounded by the header block before either of its two passes, and reads nothing through the Lisp reader. Covered scope: soundness in the one direction stated (accepted implies an address); that the recognizer accepts every conformant mailbox-list is not a theorem and is witnessed across the grammar's productions. The subject is fn-inj-decide, which books/nntp-post.lisp fn-nntp-post-step calls on the served POST path (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk through fn-own-read) and books/owner.lisp fn-own-operator-decision calls on the operator's.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the agents run's `From: yue`. Teeth in tests/acl2/injection-tests.lisp: the INN lab's POSTed article (its injected octets are what innd received) and `From: yue` refused :from-invalid; accepted and refused values across the productions; one must-fail per hypothesis. The v0 matrix row V0-POST-FROM-MAILBOX measures it on a node; no image carries it yet.

proofs.title: A relayed article changes in Path and Xref only, once, at acceptance (RFC 5537 3.6, 3.7)
proofs.statement: Over fn-peer-relayed-octets, the octets this node stores, serves and feeds on for an article a peer transferred: fn-peer-relayed-octets-change-only-path-and-xref -- removing every Path and Xref field (with its continuation lines) from what arrived and from what is stored leaves the same octets, so every other header field in order, the blank line and the body are byte-identical; fn-peer-relayed-octets-are-idempotent -- a second pass by the same node changes nothing; fn-peer-relayed-octets-carry-no-xref -- no Xref field is stored; fn-peer-relayed-octets-name-this-node-in-every-path -- when the node has a <path-identity>, every Path field of what is stored begins with it and "!" (RFC 5537 3.6 step 7, 3.7 step 6; the 3.2.1 diagnostic follows it). None has a hypothesis but the last, whose one is the identity. Each is the article-level keystone of books/path-update.lisp (fn-pu-relay-article-changes-only-path-and-xref, -is-idempotent, -leaves-no-xref, -names-the-agent-in-every-path), proved by one induction each over a walk of the raw header lines whose re-read of its own output is exact. fn-peer-injection-arguments-payload-unfolds: the payload the transfer stages for fn-node-prepare is fn-peer-relayed-octets of the received octets. Covered scope: the octets; what a reader receives is those octets (fn-durable-completion-installs-exact-pending-article, PRF-002), and the served rendering's dot-stuffing is the wire books'. An article with no Path field gets none (RFC 5537 3.7 step 1's rejection of it is open). The subjects are what the host calls: fn-peer-relayed-octets at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take, which fills fn-owner-submit-octets, the octets host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-one digests and stores; and fn-peer-injection-arguments at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide, whose staged payload the drain compares with them before the store attempt. fn-peer-relayed-octets-keep-the-received-path-tail (2026-09-24; keystone fn-pu-relay-article-keeps-the-received-path-tail, books/path-update-tail.lisp): when the node has a <path-identity>, the content of each stored Path field line, read by fn-pu-path-contents with the walk's own line classification, is the received content with <identity>!<diagnostic>! in front, or unchanged when it already begins with <identity>!; so the update prepends and the received Path is the tail. Covered scope: the first physical line of each Path field; folded continuation lines are copied and not read.
proofs.progress_note: Lane T13-conform, 2026-09-22, from the INN lab's findings 2 and 3 (fn served INN's Path without itself, and INN's Xref). Decided at acceptance, not at serving time: specs/peering.md 2.3 carries the argument. Teeth in tests/acl2/peer-inbound-tests.lisp, last section: innfeed's own TAKETHIS octets become the stored article byte for byte (Path fnA.hbox.test!!inn.hbox.test!..., no Xref), through the transfer to the durable article, with the parser's view of the result; .MISMATCH. for a peer expecting another identity; a Path line the update would push past 998 octets refused :oversize; one must-fail per hypothesis (and, for the three statements with none, the stronger statement refuted by the lab's value). The INN lab rows V0-INN-SERVING-AGENT and V0-INN-OPERATOR-POST measure it on a node; no image carries it yet.

proofs.title: A served POST's Injection-Info names the node's path-identity
proofs.statement: fn-oag-post-config-agent-is-the-path-identity: when the replayed configuration's path-identity policy is set, the posting configuration fn-oag-post-config installs (called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-config, which fn-owner-recover and fn-owner-reconfigure-complete install with fn-own-configure) has that identity's octets as its agent; unset, the agent is fn.example.invalid. fn-oag-open-pins-the-owner-config: a connection fn-ocfg-open opens (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open) at an identifier no connection already holds pins the owner's installed configuration; fn-oag-configured-open-pins-the-path-identity composes the two. fn-oag-served-post-names-the-pinned-agent: for any socket read fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix performs (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk), if the connection's served state satisfies fn-served-connp, the submission the read hands the owner, when it is an injected article, carries the Injection-Info line generated from the agent the connection pinned; the chain runs through fn-served-step, fn-served-feed, fn-served-dispatch, fn-auth-step, fn-peer-step and fn-nntp-post-step to fn-inj-injected-article-names-the-configured-agent over fn-inj-decide. Covered scope: the served POST path; the fn-served-connp premise is the served invariant the owner does not carry (the premise PRF-006 records for fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix), and no value is known on which the conclusion fails without it. fn.toml's [posting] agent is refused by run (fn-native-config-unsupported-key), so the path-identity policy is the only agent.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t6b-profile, 2026-09-22: the served-POST keystone is proved over the host-called fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix under the fn-served-connp premise; tests/acl2/owner-agent-tests.lisp carries a reachable witness built as the host builds it (a replayed history with the policy set path-identity delta, fn-oag-post-config, fn-ocfg-open, one POST read through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix whose queued article says Injection-Info: hbox.ember.software) and a must-fail per hypothesis, with a refuting value for the identity and freshness hypotheses and none known for the served premise. The image measurement is tests/test_native_profile.py and V0-NODE-PROFILE.

proofs.title: The native service log says what the reply says, one line per event
proofs.statement: fn-olog-served-post-line-says-accepted-iff-durable: the line host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-outcome renders for a served submission begins with the word accepted exactly when fn-own-outcome-completion of the host's word is :durable, the completion fn-own-outcome renders into the 240; a host word alone never makes it say accepted. fn-olog-control-post-line-says-the-control-result: the control line's first word is the word of fn-own-control-outcome-result, the value the control reply carries. fn-olog-served-post-line-is-one-line, fn-olog-control-post-line-is-one-line and fn-olog-connection-line-is-one-line: no line contains CR or LF, whatever octets the Message-ID, agent or peer name held. fn-olog-staging-cleanup-line-is-one-line: the line host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-staging-cleanup renders for an error fnn-publish's best-effort staging cleanup swallowed after the record is durable contains no CR or LF, whatever the stage path or the OS error text held; that the host writes it exactly once per swallowed error is measured by the NNTP probe's record-stage-unlinked EIO row, not proved. Covered scope: the rendered octets; that host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-log writes them and one LF to the file run opened append-only is measured by tests/test_native_profile.py, not proved. bp-app-refusal-line-says-refused-iff-refused: the BP application receiver's line for a transfer it did not accept (host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-deliver, through host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-refusal-log) begins with refused exactly when the receiver answered :refused or :clock-unusable, so a busy owner reads deferred and an unknown word uncertain; fn-olog-bp-app-refusal-line-is-one-line: that line holds no CR or LF, and it carries the application planner's reason field. Covered scope: the rendered octets; that host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-log writes them and one LF to the file run opened append-only is measured by tests/test_native_profile.py, not proved.
proofs.progress_note: Lane t6b-profile, 2026-09-22: the keystones have no hypotheses; tests/acl2/owner-log-tests.lisp evaluates each renderer on a real injected decision and a real control decision, and its must-fails name the weaker statements a host-word log would satisfy (the line echoes the host word; the control line uses the served classification) with the refuting owner evaluated beside each.

proofs.title: Bounded canonical BPv7 status-report payload codec
proofs.statement: For every fn-bpn-reportp payload, fn-bpn-report-decode of fn-bpn-report-encode returns that report and no trailing octets (fn-bpn-report-decode-of-encode); valid reports encode in at most 1194 octets (fn-bpn-report-encode-length-bound), below the decoder 4096-octet preflight, and every accepted input re-encodes byte-for-byte (fn-bpn-report-accepted-input-is-canonical). This covers RFC 9171 section 6.1.1 whole and fragment payloads, four assertions, optional requested times, and local reason codes 0 to 11. Reports are remote observations only; node-machine generation, correlation, consumption and release authority are outside this codec claim.
proofs.note: D1a codec source and its tests have ACL2 certification, including a maximal-profile witness and rejected malformed/noncanonical vectors. No native node path calls this codec yet. These component theorems are therefore not credited as requirement keystone events under the actual-caller rule; D1b/D2 generation and consumption remain open. The evidence records the component claims without implying a served implementation.

proofs.title: TCPCL final acknowledgement follows the durable delivery disposition
proofs.statement: The exact native fn-tcl-host-drive caller emits final END ACKs only immediately before matching :bundle-received events; at each such event, the ordered held messages satisfy fn-tcl-held-final-ackp. The host-called fn-tcl-delivery-plan then releases that ACK only for (:accepted path-or-nil), replaces it with XFER_REFUSE for definitive (:refused reason), and withholds it for (:uncertain reason). The source-level proof does not establish the physical FNBS barrier, raw Lisp execution, or socket delivery.
proofs.progress_note: ACL2 8.7 certified the exact host-drive event order, ordered held-list projection and conditional delivery plan. Reachable witnesses cover coalesced prior-transfer partial ACK/refusal, two completed bundles in one read, and missing-held/path-type counterexamples. Native source executes the selected message list; combined-image A2 callback runtime remains pending.

proofs.title: BP persisted age anchors are compared only within a durable boot domain
proofs.statement: The host-called fn-bpnf-clock-domain-plan returns :same only when a valid saved FNBS kind-6 frame decodes to the exact canonical current Linux boot ID; a different boot fences regardless of the numeric monotonic reading, and a missing marker with legacy obligations fences rather than renewing or expiring them. The 82-byte marker roundtrip and served guards are certified. The host's boot-ID observation, physical barriers, and combined-image caller still require native evidence, and cross-boot reanchoring remains open.
proofs.progress_note: The exact startup planner and canonical kind-6 marker are ACL2-owned, guard verified, and focused-book certified. Concrete witnesses include same-boot restart, both directions of incomparable new-boot uptime, legacy outbound and received rows, malformed marker, invalid observed ID, and a crash in the publisher link window. Native combined-image and physical clock/barrier evidence remain pending. A mismatched or legacy domain is an explicit lifecycle fence, not completed reboot recovery.

proofs.title: Native authored carrier receives the local NNTP injection trace without changing signed source
proofs.statement: For any nonnil result of the exact ACL2 fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets called by host/native/hybrid-control.lisp, fn-hsig-injected-carrier-retains-exact-signed-source proves the authenticated authored source is a suffix of the received octets, and fn-hsig-injected-carrier-is-a-news-injection proves the received octets satisfy the ordinary fn-inj-reinjectionp grammar for the rendered portable carrier, configured agent and projected Message-ID. The native event constructor accepts only the same injected bytes. This is an ACL2 byte-projection claim under a successful injection decision; it does not prove cryptographic primitives, filesystem durability, or peer I/O.
proofs.progress_note: The source-matched ACL2 book/test and dependent Store tests passed on hbox. The positive fixture constructs a real schema-1 injected event and replays its exact source; closed injection and pathless carrier witnesses fail the conclusions when the successful-injection premise is removed. The combined native two-owner peering/restart test awaits the shared image.

proofs.title: Exact-source topic metadata candidate is bounded and canonical
proofs.statement: The native topic-inspect-carrier command passes only the exact source returned after hybrid-carrier verification to fn-th-host-inspect-source. Successful inspection binds to exactly one FN-Topic field in that parsed source and its canonical raw physical lines. Every valid root, control, or report constructor encodes within 1,531 binary octets and 39 items; decoding its encoding recovers the constructor. The canonical folded field renderer emits lines of at most 85 octets. Accepted decoder bytes are canonical. This establishes no topic anchor or admission.
proofs.progress_note: ACL2 8.7 certified the codec, general constructor bound/inverse, host-called authored raw-line binding, canonical folded-field line bound, and max-profile/negative tests at exact digests on hbox. The full-envelope native saved-image max-profile gate remains pending; no topic admission claim is made.

proofs.title: Consumer projection equals the completed Store prefix through publication and crash replay
proofs.statement: Under fn-csi-full-relationp, the actual decoded Store dispatcher fn-snrt-step preserves the phase-aware relation for every event (fn-csi-store-step-preserves-full-relation). The relation equates the carried consumer projection with strict replay of the completed dense Store prefix, checks a linked unfinished candidate before finish, erases the process projection on crash, and reconstructs it from physical records on recovery. Induction over fn-snrt-run yields arbitrary finite mixed traces; a corrupted carried projection refutes the premise in the test book. This component covers logical Store transitions and admissible crash images, not a host-observed syscall refinement or served consumer call.
proofs.progress_note: The logical Store invariant and test roots are certified in scope. Native image 1d26e01f separately witnesses local-owner poll, advancing ACK/reopen, selected packing and fenced clone cursor recovery. Those tests do not prove syscall refinement or the consumer-owned transaction/ACK/reply join; general remote policy and two-store composition remain open. The current topic/consumer composition now certifies the actual :prepare-topic consumer-relation arm and a reachable bootstrap/register, topic admin/anchor/report, observed-reopen trace with ACK unchanged; the hbox source-matched scope is in planning/evidence/consumer-topic-store-trace-2026-09-24.md. This adds no served-path or physical durability claim.

proofs.title: Topic candidate author and root declaration bind to verified historical context
proofs.statement: The native topic inspector calls the ACL2 selector with exact source, principal and ordered keys returned by hybrid verification. A selected root is marked controller-matched only when its declared controller equals that principal and its declared keyset ID equals the ACL2 subject identity of the canonical principal/key snapshot. Reports obtain their author reference from that same verified context, not metadata or From. For a retained schema-1 event the historical selector first requires the T10 exact-source/carrier/keyring-snapshot binding; no topic admission or succession decision follows.
proofs.progress_note: The selector and accepted-event wrapper plus matching/mismatching principal, changed-key, From, relay and unbound historical event witnesses certify on hbox at the lane source. A source-matched saved-image CLI run and integrated reverse closure remain pending. The native command keeps generic candidate output and explicitly reports admission=unestablished.

proofs.title: Pinned group buckets and OVER ranges refine the committed archive
proofs.statement: For a projection-consistent accepted archive, fn-gidx-listgroup-command-of-build equates indexed LISTGROUP with the archive command. For an accepted archive, maintained bucket and trie correspondence, and an OVER or XOVER keyword, fn-nntp-carried-over-range-equals-archive-command equates the actual pinned archive dispatcher with the original response for every one-argument token; invalid ranges and untagged indexes fall through. fn-gidx-number-article-of-build proves that a bucket entry resolves through the trie to the same first article as the archive scan, including the identifier and number availability gates. For ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY and STAT and every argument list, fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned-msgid-arms-are-the-scan equates the same pinned dispatcher with the scanning archive dispatcher under the trie correspondence alone. fn-own-read reaches that dispatcher through served dispatch; fn-own-relation and fn-served-connp maintain the pins across view refresh, open, feed and read. The claim excludes arbitrary tagged indexes, unindexed HDR/GROUP/NEXT/LAST/NEWNEWS, the IHAVE/CHECK history test (a scan of the live node, fn-peer-history-hasp), disk indexing, and elapsed-time performance.
proofs.progress_note: Scoped ACL2 certification and called-owner sparse/historical LISTGROUP witnesses are recorded in the group-bucket evidence. Indexed OVER/XOVER resolve selected-group bucket entries through the pinned trie; the called pinned dispatcher equality has direct reachable and malformed-state premise teeth, with redundant range, tag, bound and session assumptions removed. HDR remains on the archive fold. The native OVER/XOVER socket driver is prepared but has not run on a source-matched image; combined-image qualification and full dependent closure at integrated source remain open.

proofs.title: Experimental root-only topic admission is grounded in historical authorship and finite local policy
proofs.statement: The experimental root-only Store path selects prior T10-bound exact source and snapshot, checks installed local administrator, roster, same-topic parents and finite quota, and completes only a matching topic event. Fresh version-2 root anchors bind the exact earlier immutable administrator-install event ID and generation; historical version-1 anchors retain ID-only replay semantics and cannot be freshly staged. The owner-called report selector returns :replayed-historical only for selected earlier exact source and retained admission, without another Store event. Topic completion advances the exact Store sequence/transaction and slot-12 projection while preserving article acceptance. Observed reopen separately validates topic replay; deriving that validity for every modeled crash image from a maintained live Store relation remains open. Native v2 migration and physical publication are not yet qualified.
proofs.progress_note: Scoped v2 local proposal, Store fresh-v1 refusal, canonical event/prefix and mixed-source vector roots passed at exact bytes. Historical v1 meaning is retained. The dual-image native migration test is prepared but has not run; a v2 saved image and full affected closure remain open. The maintained topic/crash relation is under separate active proof work and is not supplied by the interim BP/byte reopen premise.

proofs.title: Local consumer status reports the scoped committed journal distance
proofs.statement: The experimental local-owner command `consumer status CONTROL ID` reports the registered consumer ACK, committed journal frontier and their event-distance from fixed committed Store projections after the same local principal, query-version and view-version scope checks used by position and poll. The diagnostic leaves owner state unchanged. For the exact host-called kind-9 FNCT codec, decoding an encoded accepted reply returns its ACK, frontier and gap when ACK and frontier are uint32 values, ACK is no greater than frontier, and gap equals frontier minus ACK; decoding an encoded refused, uncertain or fault reply returns that status with empty fields under the constrained frame-digest shape. This target remains in progress because the subsequent topic/index composition requires its own native qualification. The codec theorem does not prove concrete hash security, native filesystem recovery or article unreadness/application processing; Store recovery authority remains PRF-064.
proofs.progress_note: The ACL2 local status codec, owner scope decision and native-control host test passed the scoped status/index run. The general accepted and nonaccepted kind-9 codec roundtrips and their isolating teeth certified in the selected hbox book/test roots at the exact new source bytes; these are proof-only changes to the executable codec. The earlier e160442f image passed unknown-consumer refusal, read-only status, advancing ACK and recovered status checks. The joined topic/index source has scoped certification but has not yet run on a matching saved image. The diagnostic does not assert application processing or discharge.

proofs.title: Operator-local hybrid key lifecycle preserves per-principal authority and historical verdicts
proofs.statement: The host-called local enrollment and revocation constructors require the next durable keyring generation; new hybrid-author requests use only the named principal's newest recognized enrollment, leaving unrelated principals active, while identity replay retains earlier snapshots and accepted verdicts byte-exact across rotation and revocation.
proofs.progress_note: The per-principal selector, next-generation event constructors and versioned tombstone are implemented. Completed kind-3 Store-node theorems equate the post-finish selector to identity replay and preserve historical verdicts; successful recovery theorems equate the carried selector and verdicts to replay of recovered durable records. A reachable Store trace commits A1 and a kind-4 verdict, then B2, A3 rotation and A4 tombstone, checking maintained node/file and identity-sequence relations and observed reopen. Selected crash cuts before and after B2 publication distinguish absent from durable enrollment. The host calls the selector under the serialized owner. The frozen 863c2141 production image passed three targeted native lifecycle/carrier tests on scratch Stores with OpenSSL 3.5.8. proofs.title: Group names are the RFC 5536 section 3.1.4 grammar and reserved names are never created
proofs.statement: fn-record-group-namep-is-the-rfc-5536-grammar: the recognizer every host site applies admits exactly an ASCII string of 1 to 128 octets (local bound) whose octets are an RFC 5536 section 3.1.4 <newsgroup-name>; four rejection theorems name a forbidden octet, a leading dot, an empty component and a trailing dot. fn-native-admin-plan-refuses-a-reserved-group-create: a well-formed `group create NAME` whose NAME is reserved (first component "example" or the name "poster", ASCII case folded) is refused :reserved-group-name and carries no configuration delta; the subject is fn-native-admin-plan, which host/native-admin-host.lisp:7 calls. fn-native-operator-run-refuses-a-reserved-init-group: an `init` naming a reserved group in any position is never an accepted plan; the subject is fn-native-operator-run, which host/native-operator-host.lisp:19 calls, and host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-dispatch-plan exits on a non-accepted plan before any store observation. fn-native-admin-group-name-creatablep-is-the-rfc-5536-rule: a creatable name is a valid group name whose case-folded octets are not "example", do not begin "example.", and are not "poster". Covered scope: the operator and admin command paths; the initial configuration record's refusal in fn-cfg-host-initial-octets (program mode) is witnessed, not proved.
